subject: Locklane provisioning check — AuroraGen POC runway
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-21T09:02:00-07:00
Subject: Locklane provisioning check — AuroraGen POC runway

Team —

AuroraGen (Samir Patel) is pushing to start a 6-week POC that needs a predictable dedicated pool: roughly 12 A100-equivalent GPUs for sustained 8k token workloads with occasional bursts to 18 GPUs during nightly fine-tune cycles. They are late-stage and asking for a start window around 2026-06-08.

Can we confirm the following by EOD today?
- Inventory check: Are 12-18 A100-equivalent slots available in us-west for the 6/8 start window? If not, what is the nearest viable start date?
- Sweep risk: Any competing commitments or scheduled maintenance that could impact availability in that window?
- Contingency: If we cannot guarantee the pool, can we offer a hybrid plan (dedicated + burst to shared with pre-warmed nodes) and what SLA/lift would that imply?

I've attached a draft capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx with AuroraGen's requested profile and the initial MOU draft. Samir copied procurement@auroragen.ai — they expect a short mutual action plan once we confirm capacity.

Critical ask: I need a crisp go/no-go + one-paragraph recommended fallback to share with Samir by 3pm PT so we don't lose momentum.

Thanks —
Neha Kapoor
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

Attachments: capacity_matrix_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet), auroragen_mou_draft.pdf (pdf)
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: 2026-05-21T10:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locklane provisioning check — AuroraGen POC runway

Neha —

Quick inventory readout: current us-west committed pools have ~24 A100-equivalent nodes nominally free across Dedicated and pre-warmed standby this quarter, but there's a planned driver stack upgrade on 2026-06-06 that will require a 36-hour rolling maintenance on a subset of nodes (we can avoid the maintenance window for the specific fleet if we pin capacity). Two notes:

1) If we pin 12 GPUs from the Dedicated pool (reserve with a soft-hold), we can guarantee availability for the 6/8 start — but pinning requires a 4-week minimum billing commitment change on the contract side.
2) For bursts to 18 GPUs nightly, we can serve via a temporary carve-out from pre-warmed standby; that will increase the cost delta by ~22% (due to pre-warm utilization and burst uplift).

I recommend: soft-hold 12 GPUs in us-west + documented burst uplift for nights. Ops needs a signed MOU or internal approval note to convert the soft-hold to a billable reservation.

I'll ping Ops for a final technical confirmation and timeline.

—Rishi
Head of Capacity Planning, Redwood Inference
From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Patel <samir@auroragen.ai>; procurement@auroragen.ai
Date: 2026-05-21T13:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locklane provisioning check — AuroraGen POC runway

Samir / AuroraGen —

Thanks for the details earlier. Quick clarification on the workload: you mentioned \"8k token sustained with nightly fine-tune bursts\" — can you confirm average request concurrency (# of simultaneous sessions) and whether KV-cache snapshot persistence between runs is required? These materially affect the slot sizing and whether we need NVMe-local scratch.

Proposed immediate path (to keep timeline):
- Redwood can soft-hold a 12-GPU dedicated slice in us-west for the 6/8 start.
- Nightly burst to 18 GPUs is supported via pre-warmed standby; we will document a burst uplift in the MOU (~22%).
- To convert the soft-hold to a committed reservation (and avoid the 06/06 maintenance risk), we need a signed MOU by 2026-05-26.

If procurement can sign a 4-week minimum reservation addendum we will finalize node pinning and freeze the kernel/driver image for that pool.

Action: Samir — can procurement confirm concurrency and sign-off timeline?

Best,
Aditya Rao
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwood.ai
From: Samir Patel <samir@auroragen.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@auroragen.ai, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-05-21T15:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Locklane provisioning check — AuroraGen POC runway

Aditya / Neha / Team —

Thanks — confirmed concurrency: expected 10 concurrent sessions peak (6–8 average) during business hours; nightly fine-tune is single-job but heavy (can live with ephemeral KV caches, no snapshot persistence required).

Procurement confirms they can sign the 4-week addendum by 2026-05-25. We'll route the MOU to our legal and loop back. If you can provide a one-paragraph fallback (hybrid flow + cost uplift) for my CFO, that will speed approval.

I'll also attach a short infra appendix from our side by EOD that lists dataset sizes and expected egress patterns.

—Samir Patel
VP Product, AuroraGen
procurement@auroragen.ai (copied)
